root_cause_label: Manual Dependency Stripping and Serial Install Loop
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent chose a fatally slow strategy of stripping version constraints one-by-one and installing dependencies serially to work around Python 3.12 incompatibilities, consuming the entire step budget without completing installation, then restarted the same loop from scratch near the end.
t_err_evidence: Step 14: agent edits setup.py to strip 'matplotlib==3.1.1' to 'matplotlib' after a single pip install failure, committing to a manual per-dependency constraint-removal approach rather than adopting a more efficient strategy (e.g., using a compatible Python version, targeting PyTorch-only, or installing with --no-deps and patching setup.py globally up front).
t_commit_evidence: Step 21: agent explicitly decides to 'install spinningup dependencies manually, one-by-one' starting with mpi4py, locking in a serial installation loop that historically took 40+ steps just to reach torch (which itself kept timing out), making task completion within the remaining ~100 steps essentially impossible.
t_surface_evidence: Step 99: first attempted training run (python -m spinup.run ppo ...) fails with NameError: name 'tf' is not defined in mpi_tf.py, making the installation failure visibly observable.
trigger_explanation: The agent operated under the false premise that stripping version constraints one at a time and installing dependencies serially would eventually yield a working installation within the step budget. In reality, the approach consumed 40+ steps just to reach torch (which repeatedly timed out on download), and the agent never verified that TensorFlow 1.x—the core dependency driving the mpi_tf.py issue—was even installable on Python 3.12 before committing to this path.
forewarning_evidence: Step 15: after removing tensorflow constraint, pip immediately errors on torch==1.3.1 incompatibility, signaling the cascading nature of the dependency conflicts. Steps 19-20: torch download times out at 530MB, foreshadowing that the serial per-package approach will be extremely slow. Steps 23-25: gym[atari] installation itself times out repeatedly, further confirming the time-sink nature of this approach.
